props.headline: Distributed SQL, No App-Side Sharding
props.subheadline: Vitess and PlanetScale shard MySQL at the middleware layer, so your application owns shard routing. TiDB is a native distributed SQL database: transparent sharding, cross-shard transactions, and HTAP in one system.

items.title: Transparent Auto-Sharding
items.description: TiDB auto-splits data into ranges and rebalances transparently — no shard keys or resharding logic in your app.

items.title: Cross-Shard ACID
items.description: Distributed transactions and cross-shard queries in one system — no application-level routing or migration.

items.title: HTAP in One Engine
items.description: Run analytics on live data with TiFlash — no separate analytics stack for SaaS, fintech, or AI workloads.

items.title: Distributed ACID Transactions
items.description: TiDB provides distributed ACID transactions across the entire cluster. Cross-shard transactions and queries are a known constraint of MySQL-sharding approaches like Vitess and PlanetScale.

items.title: Transparent Rebalancing
items.description: TiDB's operator and transparent rebalancing remove much of the recurring resharding toil that grows with a Vitess topology.

items.title: Kubernetes-Native
items.description: Full lifecycle management via TiDB Operator — no manual shard topology changes or routing updates.

items.title: Auto-Scaling
items.description: Scale compute and storage independently without application downtime or shard key redesign.

items.title: Pure Partitioning Workloads
items.description: If your scaling need is primarily partitioning a workload across shards, and you explicitly do not need cross-shard distributed transactions, strong cross-shard consistency, or HTAP, Vitess may be the simpler local choice.

items.q: Is Vitess or TiDB better for scaling MySQL?
items.a: For teams that need cross-shard consistency, cross-shard queries, or HTAP, TiDB is the better choice. For pure partitioning without those needs, Vitess can suffice.

items.q: Is TiDB a good PlanetScale alternative?
items.a: Yes. PlanetScale is managed Vitess, so it inherits the same application-side sharding model. TiDB replaces that with native, transparent distributed SQL: no shard keys in your app, cross-shard ACID transactions, and HTAP in one engine.
Cross-shard transactions and queries are limited in MySQL-sharding approaches. TiDB provides distributed ACID across the cluster.
Yes — TiDB provides full MySQL protocol and syntax compatibility.

items.q: Which is easier to operate on Kubernetes?
items.a: TiDB's transparent auto-sharding and Kubernetes operator reduce the resharding and routing work that Vitess pushes to the application team.

items.q: When should a team replace MySQL sharding with distributed SQL?
items.a: When resharding pain, cross-shard query complexity, rising operational burden, or stronger consistency needs outweigh the flexibility of middleware sharding.
